visuals.heading: Why This Matters Before You Read Further

items.text: Project management is a genuinely different career, and the PMP question is genuinely different from anything in those product-management guides.

Project management is one of the few career tracks that genuinely transfers across very different industries, because the core skill (delivering defined work under constraints) does not change even though the constraints themselves do.
The order below is not alphabetical or a prestige ranking; it runs by real growth and growth headroom.
Consulting comes second, not third, because it is the track most likely to scale into an independent practice with several clients rather than one employer's pay band.

blocks.heading: CAPM and PRINCE2: the Real Alternatives

items.text: PMP is not the only credential in project management, and it is not always the right first move.
Issued by PMI, the same body behind PMP.

Before you spend money on PMP prep or commit years to this track, run yourself through the same four-part check that applies to any real career decision: your fit, your situation, the job market and AI-proofing.
Do you actually enjoy the unglamorous core of the job, chasing status updates, managing a budget line by line, and holding people accountable to a date they did not choose.
If what excites you is deciding what gets built, not delivering what was decided, that is closer to product management than project management.

Core skills: customer research, prioritisation, business judgment, roadmap thinking

blocks.heading: PMP Eligibility: the Real Hour Requirement
rows: Bachelor's degree (or global equivalent)
36 months (3 years) leading and directing projects, within the last 8 years
35 hours of formal project management education
No bachelor's degree (high school diploma or equivalent)

blocks.heading: PMP Worth It Early-Career or Only Later
rows: 0-2 years experience, no project-leading role yet
Not yet. You are not eligible to sit the exam. Focus on building real coordination experience and consider CAPM instead.
2-3 years, close to but not past the experience threshold
Start the 35-hour education requirement now; hold off on the exam fee until the experience hours are actually documented and complete.
3+ years with real project-leading experience, targeting IT, construction, or consulting
Yes.
Already senior with a strong delivery track record
Optional. Track record and stakeholder trust already do most of the work; PMP adds a formal signal but is no longer the main lever.

blocks.heading: What Project Managers Actually Earn in India
rows: Fresher or coordinator-level (0-2 years)
Rs 7-9 LPA
Usually a project coordinator or associate PM title, not a standalone "Project Manager" title yet, regardless of industry.
IT / software project manager, mid-experience
Rs 17-18 LPA average
One of the higher-paying tracks; senior IT project managers commonly move into the mid-20s LPA range.
Construction project manager
Roughly Rs 6-30 LPA, ~Rs 10-18 LPA typical
Wider range than IT, driven heavily by project scale, city, and whether the employer is a developer, contractor, or consultancy.
Senior project manager, 7-9+ years, any industry
Rs 13-25 LPA+
At this stage a PMP credential, a track record of delivered projects, and stakeholder trust matter more than the industry label on the resume.

blocks.heading: Mistakes People Make Chasing PMP Too Early

figures.label: Relevant Experience Window
figures.source: PMP requires 36 months of documented project-leading experience with a degree, or 60 months without one. Spending money on PMP prep courses in your first year wastes the training window; that 35-hour education requirement stays valid for years, so it is not wasted, but the certification itself cannot be earned yet.
